question: What is the chemical name of plaster of paris?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Plaster of Paris**/**Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate (CaSO₄·1/2H₂O):**

__
 
• It is a **white powdery substance** that is commonly **used **in the **medical field for casting broken bones.**
 
• It is **created by heating gypsum**, **a mineral found in sedimentary rocks.**
 
• When m**ixed with water, it forms a paste that hardens quickly** and is used in construction for creating molds and sculptures.
 
• It is a**lso used in the food industry as a coagulant** for tofu and as a calcium supplement in certain types of bread.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calcium hypochlorite (Ca(ClO)₂):**

 
 
• It is a white solid, although commercial samples appear yellow.
 
• It is commonly **used to sanitize public swimming pools **and **disinfect drinking water.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃):**
 
 
• Similar to the minerals calcite and aragonite, it is a common component** found in rocks**, particularly in **chalk **and limestone, **eggshells**, gastropod shells, **shellfish skeletons**, and **pearls**.
 
• It is the **primary component of agricultural lime** and is created when carbonate ions and calcium ions in hard water combine to form limescale.
 
• It has **medical use** as a **calcium supplemen**t or as an antacid.
 
 
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• It is commonly known as **quicklime or burnt lime.**
 
• It is a white, caustic, alkaline, crystalline solid at room temperature.
 
• It is used in the **production of cement, paper, and steel.**
